title: Development of a Retractable CMOS Camera for Transmission Electron Microscope
content: Image sensors are commonly used to record transmission electron microscope (TEM) images as digital data. In an indirect detection TEM camera, the electrons carrying sample information are converted to visible light by a phosphor, and the image is then captured by an image sensor. There are two main types of indirect detection cameras. The fiber-coupled camera uses a fiber optic plate (FOP) coated with phosphors, while the lens-coupled camera uses lenses to project the fluorescent pattern onto the image sensor. In the fiber-coupled camera, the FOP and image sensor are bonded together, and the FOP directly transmits the fluorescent pattern to the image sensor. Therefore, a fiber-coupled camera has a numerical aperture of 1 and can achieve higher detection sensitivity compared to a lens-coupled camera.
